title: WPSB/283/2019 of DEEPAK KUMAR JOSHI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 283 of 2019 (S/B)
Deepak Kumar Joshi .......Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & another ........Respondents
Present:- Mr. Dushyant Mainali, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Ms. Puja Banga, Brief Holder for the State/respondent no.1.
 Mr. B.D. Kandpal, Advocate for respondent no. 2.

Coram: Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
 Hon'ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 The petitioner was a candidate who appeared
in the Uttarakhand Civil Services Examination for the
year 2012. There are three stages for the examination.
First is the preliminary examination where initially
screening is done and only such candidates who qualify
the preliminary examination appear in the main
examination and thereafter those candidates who pass in
the main examination are called for the interview as per
their merit list.
 According to the petitioner, he had qualified
the preliminary examination as well as the main
examination and thereafter he was called for the
interview, but his name did not figure in the final
selection list. Aggrieved, the petitioner had filed a writ
petition before this Court being WPSB No. 571 of 2017
challenging the examination and the selection process,
and the manner in which marks were awarded to him.

2
The said writ petition was dismissed as withdrawn by the
Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 08.11.2017.
The order dated 08.11.2017 reads as under:-
"Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned counsel for
the petitioner seeks permission to withdraw
this writ petition with liberty to file a fresh writ
petition.
2. Writ petition is dismissed as
withdrawn with liberty as above."
 Now the petitioner has again filed the present
writ petition on the ground that when he was given his
answer-sheets and after the examination he found that he
has not received the marks which he deserved in Ethics
paper. The petitioner got his Ethics paper examined on
his own from one Dr. Aditya Kumar Gupta, who is a
professor of Delhi University. The said examiner has
evaluated the Ethics paper of the petitioner on each
question and has then come to the conclusion that on
various questions, the petitioner has been given low
marks, whereas he deserved higher marks. Now the
petitioner prays that based on this report, his papers be
re-evaluated!
 This prayer of the petitioner is totally
misconceived and rather fanciful. If what the petitioner
wants is permitted, there will be no end for the re-evaluation or re-examination process. Admittedly, there is
no provision in the Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission Rules for re-evaluation of papers and
therefore the request of the petitioner was rightly declined
in the first place.

3
 The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pramod
Kumar Srivastava vs. Chairman, Bihar Public Service
Commission, Patna and others, reported in (2004) 6
SCC 714, has held that where there is no provision for re-evaluation, such a prayer cannot be granted.
 In the present case, however, the petitioner
has in fact gone many steps ahead. He got his answer-sheets examined by a professor of Delhi University, who
has re-evaluated the performance of the petitioner and
has said that the petitioner has not given the marks
which he deserved. On the basis of this, the petitioner
claims re-evaluation of his papers as already stated
above.
 The prayer of the petitioner cannot be granted
by this Court. The writ petition is dismissed with a cost of
Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand Only), which shall be
deposited by the petitioner before the Registry of this
Court within a period of three weeks from the date of
production of a certified copy of this order.
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 08.07.2019
Ankit/
